title.zh: 卷87 節義:于什門 段進 石文德 汲固 王玄威 婁提 劉渴侯
title.en: Volume 87: Morality and Righteousness: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou
title.raw: 卷87 節義:于什門 段進 石文德 汲固 王玄威 婁提 劉渴侯 Volume 87: Morality and Righteousness: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou

sentences.zh: 于什門 段進 石文德 汲固 王玄威 婁提 劉渴侯 朱長生 于提 馬八龍 門文愛 晁清 劉侯仁 石祖興 邵洪哲 王榮世 胡小虎 孫道登 李几 張安祖 王閭

translations.literal: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaohu, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaohu, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü.

sentences.zh: 大義重於至聞自日人。

translations.literal: Great righteousness is heavier than the utmost fame, since the day of men. The received text of these nine characters is corrupt and cannot be reconstructed.
translations.idiomatic: That great righteousness outweighs renown has been understood since antiquity, though the opening line is corrupt in the received text.

sentences.zh: [2]慕之者蓋希，行之者實寡。

translations.literal: Those who admire it are probably few; those who practice it are truly scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Few indeed admire it, and still fewer put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 至於輕生蹈節，臨難如歸，殺身成仁，死而無悔，自非耿介苦心之人，鬱怏激氣之士，亦何能若斯。

translations.literal: As for lightly casting away life to uphold principle, facing hardship as though returning home, killing the body to complete humanity, and dying without regret—unless one were a man of upright, bitter purpose or a gentleman seething with pent indignation, how could one act thus?
translations.idiomatic: To treat life lightly for the sake of integrity, to meet peril as though going home, to give one's life to fulfill humaneness and die without regret—only a man of unbending, anguished resolve, or one whose spirit burns with thwarted passion, could do such things.

sentences.zh: 僉列之傳，名節義云。

translations.literal: All are listed in this biography; fame, integrity, and righteousness are its theme.
translations.idiomatic: They are gathered here in a single collective biography devoted to fame, integrity, and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 于簡，字什門，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jian, courtesy name Shenmen, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian, whose courtesy name was Shenmen, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 太宗時為謁者，使喻馮跋。

translations.literal: Under Taizong he served as usher and was sent as envoy to instruct Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan he served as usher and was dispatched to deliver the court's message to Feng Ba.

sentences.zh: 及至和龍，住外舍不入，使人謂跋曰：「大魏皇帝有詔，須馮主出受，然後敢入。」

translations.literal: When he reached Helong, he lodged in an outer residence and would not enter, sending someone to tell Ba, "The Great Wei emperor has an edict; the Lord of Feng must come out to receive it—only then do I dare enter."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Helong he stayed in an outer lodge and refused to go in, sending word to Feng Ba: "The emperor of Great Wei has issued an edict. Your lordship must come out to receive it; only then may I enter."

sentences.zh: 跋使人牽逼令入，見跋不拜，跋令人按其項。

translations.literal: Ba had men drag and force him to enter. Seeing Ba, he did not bow; Ba had someone press down on his neck.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba's men seized and hustled him inside. When he saw Feng Ba he would not bow, and Feng Ba ordered someone to press down on his neck.

sentences.zh: 什門曰：「馮主拜受詔，吾自以賓主致敬，何須苦見逼也！」

translations.literal: Shenmen said, "When the Lord of Feng bows to receive the edict, I myself will pay the courtesy due between host and guest—why must you torment me so!"
translations.idiomatic: Shenmen said, "When my lord of Feng bows to receive the edict, I will offer the respect proper between host and guest. Why torment me like this?"

sentences.zh: 與跋往復，聲氣厲然，初不撓屈。

translations.literal: He and Ba went back and forth; his voice and bearing were fierce, and from the first he did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He and Feng Ba argued back and forth, his tone fierce throughout, and he never once gave way.

sentences.zh: 既而跋止什門。

translations.literal: Presently Ba detained Shenmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Feng Ba held Shenmen prisoner.

sentences.zh: 什門於羣眾之中，回身背跋，被袴後襠以辱之。

translations.literal: Shenmen, in the midst of the crowd, turned his body with his back to Ba, put on trousers backward, and exposed his rear to shame him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the assembled crowd Shenmen turned his back on Feng Ba, pulled on his trousers with the seat to the front, and presented his backside to insult him.

sentences.zh: 既見拘留，隨身衣裳敗壞略盡，蟣虱被體。

translations.literal: Once detained, the clothes on his person were nearly all ruined, and lice and nits covered his body.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was held captive, the clothes he wore were nearly destroyed, and his body was covered with lice.

sentences.zh: 跋遺以衣服，什門拒而不受。

translations.literal: Ba sent him clothes; Shenmen refused and would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba sent him clothing, but Shenmen refused to take it.

sentences.zh: 和龍人皆歎曰：「雖古烈士，無以過也！」

translations.literal: The people of Helong all sighed, "Even the martyrs of old could not surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: The people of Helong all marveled: "Even the heroes of antiquity could not have done better!"

sentences.zh: 歷二十四年，[3]後馮文通上表稱臣，乃送什門歸。

translations.literal: Twenty-four years passed; later Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four years passed. When Feng Wentong at last submitted a memorial professing vassalage, Shenmen was sent back.

sentences.zh: 拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 世祖下詔曰：「什門奉使和龍，值狂豎肆虐，勇志壯厲，不為屈節，雖昔蘇武何以加之。」

translations.literal: Shizu issued an edict saying, "Shenmen was sent on mission to Helong and encountered a mad villain's tyranny; his courage and will were fierce and strong, and he would not compromise his integrity—even the Su Wu of old could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu issued an edict: "Shenmen served as envoy at Helong when a reckless usurper ran riot. His courage and resolve were magnificent, and he would not bend his integrity. Not even Su Wu of old could have done more."

sentences.zh: 賜羊千口、帛千匹，進為上大夫，策告宗廟，頒示天下，咸使聞也。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk, promoted to senior grand master, and the honor was reported to the ancestral temple and proclaimed throughout the realm so that all might hear.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk, promoted to senior grand master, and the court reported the honor to the ancestral temple and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 段進，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Duan Jin—of what place he was is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jin was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，為白道守將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign he was garrison commander of Baidao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Taiwu's reign he served as garrison commander of Baidao.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕大檀入塞，圍之，力屈被執。

translations.literal: The Rouran khan Datan entered the frontier, besieged him, and when his strength failed he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan Datan raided across the border, besieged him, and when resistance failed took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 進抗聲大罵，遂為賊殺。

translations.literal: Jin answered with a loud voice and great curses, and was thereupon killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jin shouted back and reviled them at the top of his voice, and the enemy killed him.

sentences.zh: 世祖愍之，追贈安北將軍，賜爵顯美侯，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Shizu pitied him and posthumously enfeoffed him as General Who Pacifies the North, granting the title Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu mourned him and posthumously appointed him General Who Pacifies the North, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Xianmei with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 石文德，河中蒲坂人也，[4]有行義。

translations.literal: Shi Wende was a man of Puban in Hezhong; he possessed conduct and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wende came from Puban in Hezhong and was known for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 真君初，縣令黃宣在任喪亡，宣單貧無期親，文德祖父苗以家財殯葬，持服三年，奉養宣妻二十餘載。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenjun era the magistrate Huang Xuan died in office. Xuan was alone and poor, with no close kin; Wende's grandfather Miao buried him at family expense, observed mourning for three years, and supported Xuan's wife for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenjun period the county magistrate Huang Xuan died in office. Xuan was poor and without near kin. Wende's grandfather Miao buried him at his own expense, wore mourning for three years, and supported Xuan's wife for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 及亡，又衰絰斂祔，率禮無闕。

translations.literal: When she died, he again wore hemp and performed encoffinment and joint burial, observing the rites without omission.
translations.idiomatic: When she in turn died, he again donned mourning garb, encoffined her, and buried her beside her husband, observing every rite without lapse.

sentences.zh: 自苗逮文德，刺史守令卒官者，制服送之。

translations.literal: From Miao down to Wende, whenever a provincial inspector or magistrate died in office, they donned mourning and escorted the body.
translations.idiomatic: From Miao down through Wende, whenever a provincial inspector or county magistrate died in office, the family wore mourning and saw the body off.

sentences.zh: 五世同居，閨門雍睦。

translations.literal: Five generations dwelt together; within the gates harmony prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations lived under one roof, and the household was harmonious throughout.

sentences.zh: 又梁州上言天水白石縣人趙令安、孟蘭彊等，四世同居，行著州里。

translations.literal: Liang province also reported that Zhao Ling'an, Meng Lanqiang, and others of Baishi county in Tianshui had dwelt together for four generations, their conduct renowned in the district.
translations.idiomatic: Liang province also reported that Zhao Ling'an, Meng Lanqiang, and others of Baishi county in Tianshui had lived together for four generations, their conduct famed throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 詔並標牓門閭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that placards be posted at all their gates.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered commemorative placards posted at each of their gates.

sentences.zh: 汲固，東郡梁城人也。

translations.literal: Ji Gu was a man of Liangcheng in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Gu came from Liangcheng in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 為兗州從事。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 刺史李式坐事被收，吏民皆送至河上。

translations.literal: The inspector Li Shi was arrested for an offense, and officials and commoners all escorted him to the river.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial inspector Li Shi was arrested for an offense, and officials and commoners alike escorted him as far as the river.

sentences.zh: 時式子憲生始滿月，式大言於眾曰：「程嬰、杵臼何如人也！」

translations.literal: At that time Shi's son Xian had just been born and was only a month old. Shi spoke loudly before the crowd: "What sort of men were Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi's son Xian had just been born and was barely a month old. Shi cried out before the crowd: "What manner of men were Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu!"

sentences.zh: 固曰：「今古豈殊。」

translations.literal: Gu said, "How can past and present differ?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Gu replied, "Past and present are not so different."

sentences.zh: 遂便潛還，不復回顧，徑來入城，於式婦閨抱憲歸藏之。

translations.literal: He then stole back without once looking behind, went straight into the city, entered the women's quarters of Shi's wife, took Xian in his arms, and returned to hide him.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away at once without a backward glance, went straight into the city, entered Shi's wife's inner quarters, took the infant Xian in his arms, and hid him away.

sentences.zh: 及捕者收憲屬，有一婢產男，母以婢兒授之。

translations.literal: When the captors came to seize those belonging to Xian, a maid had borne a son; the mother gave the maid's child in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When the search party came for Xian's kin, a maid had just given birth to a boy, and the mother handed over the maid's child in his stead.

sentences.zh: 事尋泄，固乃攜憲逃遁，遇赦始歸。

translations.literal: The matter was soon exposed; Gu then carried Xian and fled, returning only when an amnesty was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The ruse was soon discovered. Gu fled with Xian and did not return until a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 憲即為固長育至十餘歲，恒呼固夫婦為郎婆。

translations.literal: Xian was thereupon raised by Gu until he was more than ten years old, always calling Gu and his wife "Father and Mother Gu."
translations.idiomatic: Gu raised Xian to his teens, and the boy always addressed Gu and his wife as Father and Mother Gu.

sentences.zh: 後高祐為兗州刺史，嘉固節義，以為主簿。

translations.literal: Later Gao You became inspector of Yan province, admired Gu's integrity and righteousness, and appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gao You became inspector of Yan province, he admired Gu's loyalty and appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 王玄威，恒農北陝人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanwei was a man of Beishan in Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanwei came from Beishan in Hengnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 顯祖崩，玄威立草廬於州城門外，衰裳蔬粥，哭踴無時。

translations.literal: When Xianzu died, Xuanwei erected a thatched hut outside the prefectural gate, wore hemp garments and ate plain vegetables and gruel, and wept and stamped without regard to time.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen died, Xuanwei built a grass hut outside the prefectural gate, wore hemp mourning dress, lived on vegetables and gruel, and wept and stamped in grief without cease.

sentences.zh: 刺史苟頹以事表聞。

translations.literal: The inspector Gou Tui reported the matter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial inspector Gou Tui reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔令問狀，玄威稱：「先帝統御萬國，慈澤被於蒼生，含氣之類莫不仰賴，玄威不勝悲慕，中心知此，不知禮式。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered inquiry into the circumstances. Xuanwei stated, "The late emperor ruled the myriad states; his kindly grace covered the living masses, and every breathing creature looked up to him. Xuanwei cannot bear his grief and longing; in my heart I know this, but I do not know the forms of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered an inquiry. Xuanwei replied: "The late emperor ruled all lands; his kindness reached every living soul, and all who draw breath depended on him. I cannot contain my grief and longing. I feel this in my heart but do not know the proper forms of mourning."

sentences.zh: 詔問玄威欲有所訴，聽為表列。

translations.literal: The edict asked whether Xuanwei wished to present any petition and permitted him to set it forth in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The edict asked whether he wished to submit any request and allowed him to set it out in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 玄威云：「聞諱悲號，竊謂臣子同例，無所求謁。」

translations.literal: Xuanwei said, "On hearing the tabooed name I wail in grief; I privately consider that ministers and sons share the same rule, and I have nothing to request or petition for."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwei said, "Hearing the late emperor's name I can only wail. I take it that subject and son are alike in this, and I have nothing to ask of the throne."

sentences.zh: 及至百日，乃自竭家財，設四百人齋會。

translations.literal: When the hundredth day came, he exhausted his family wealth to hold a vegetarian feast for four hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: On the hundredth day he spent his entire family fortune to provide a vegetarian feast for four hundred people.

sentences.zh: 忌日，又設百僧供。

translations.literal: On the anniversary of death he again provided offerings for a hundred monks.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of the emperor's death he again provided offerings for a hundred monks.

sentences.zh: 至大除日，詔送白紬袴褶一具，與玄威釋服，下州令表異焉。

translations.literal: When the day of full mourning's end arrived, an edict sent one set of white silk trousers and jacket, released Xuanwei from mourning, and ordered the province to report his exceptional conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the period of full mourning ended, the court sent a set of white silk trousers and jacket, released him from mourning dress, and ordered the province to record his exceptional conduct.

sentences.zh: 婁提，代人也。

translations.literal: Lou Ti was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ti came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時為內三郎。

translations.literal: Under Xianzu he served as inner third-rank guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he served as an inner palace guard of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 顯祖暴崩，提謂人曰：「聖主升遐，安用活為！」

translations.literal: When Xianzu died suddenly, Ti said to others, "The sage has ascended—what use is living!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died suddenly, Lou Ti said to those around him, "Our sage lord has departed—why should I go on living?"

sentences.zh: 遂引佩刀自刺，幾至於死。

translations.literal: He then drew his girdle knife and stabbed himself, nearly dying.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the dagger at his belt and stabbed himself, coming near death.

sentences.zh: 文明太后詔賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an edict granting two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an edict granting him two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 時有敕勒部人蛭拔寅兄地于，坐盜食官馬，依制命死。

translations.literal: At that time a man of the Chile tribe, Zhi Bayin, and his elder brother Diyu were sentenced to death for stealing and eating government horses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time two men of the Chile tribe, Zhi Bayin and his elder brother Diyu, were sentenced to death for stealing and eating government horses.

sentences.zh: 拔寅自誣己殺，兄又云實非弟殺，兄弟爭死，辭不能定。

translations.literal: Bayin falsely confessed that he himself had killed; the elder brother also said that in truth it was not the younger who had killed. The brothers vied to die, and their statements could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Bayin falsely confessed to the killing himself, while his brother insisted that the younger man had not done it. The two brothers each claimed guilt, and the court could not decide between their accounts.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔原之。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued an edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict pardoning them both.

sentences.zh: 劉渴侯，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Liu Kehou—of what place he was is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kehou was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 禀性剛烈。

translations.literal: His inborn nature was fierce and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was fierce and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為徐州後軍，以力死戰，眾寡不敵，遂禽。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served as rear army of Xuzhou, fought to the death with all his strength, was outnumbered, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe period he served in the rear guard of Xuzhou, fought to the death, was overwhelmed by superior numbers, and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 瞋目大罵，終不降屈，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Glaring with wide eyes he cursed loudly, never submitting in defeat, and was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He glared and reviled them without cease, would never yield, and the enemy killed him.

sentences.zh: 高祖贈立忠將軍、平州刺史、上庸侯，賜絹千匹、穀千斛。

translations.literal: Gaozu posthumously granted him General Who Establishes Loyalty, inspector of Ping province, and Marquis of Shangyong, with a gift of a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen posthumously appointed him General Who Establishes Loyalty, inspector of Ping province, and Marquis of Shangyong, and granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 有嚴季者，亦為軍校尉，與渴侯同殿，勢窮被執，終不降屈，後得逃還。

translations.literal: There was a Yan Ji who also served as military company commander; with Kehou he fought in the rear guard, was captured when strength failed, never submitted, and later escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A certain Yan Ji also served as military company commander. He fought in the rear with Kehou, was captured when resistance collapsed, refused to submit, and later escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 除立節將軍，賜爵五等男。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Integrity and granted the fifth-rank baronetcy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Establishes Integrity and enfeoffed as a fifth-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 朱長生及于提，並代人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti were both men of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti were both men of Dai.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，以長生為員外散騎常侍，與提俱使高車。

translations.literal: Under Gaozu, Changsheng was appointed supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and, together with Ti, was sent as envoy to the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, Changsheng was appointed supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and, together with Yu Ti, was sent on embassy to the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 至其庭，高車主阿伏至羅責長生等拜，長生拒之曰：「我天子使，安肯拜下土諸侯！」

translations.literal: When they reached the court, the Gaoche ruler Avuzhiluo demanded that Changsheng and the others bow. Changsheng refused, saying, "I am an envoy of the Son of Heaven—how could I bow to a petty lord of the lower lands!"
translations.idiomatic: At the Gaoche court their ruler Avuzhiluo demanded that Changsheng and his party bow. Changsheng refused: "I am an envoy of the Son of Heaven. How could I bow to a petty frontier lord?"

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅乃不以禮待。

translations.literal: Avuzhiluo thereupon did not treat them with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Avuzhiluo then refused them proper ceremonial treatment.

sentences.zh: 長生以金銀寶器奉之，至羅既受獻，長生曰：「為臣內附，宜盡臣禮，何得口云再拜而實不拜！」

translations.literal: Changsheng presented gold, silver, and precious vessels to him. After Avuzhiluo had accepted the tribute, Changsheng said, "As a subject who has submitted within, you ought to fulfill a subject's rites—how can you say with your mouth that you bow twice while in fact not bowing!"
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng presented gold, silver, and precious vessels as tribute. Once Avuzhiluo had accepted them, Changsheng said, "As a subject who has submitted to the court, you ought to perform a subject's obeisance. How can you say you will bow twice and then not bow at all?"

sentences.zh: 呼出帳，命眾中拜。

translations.literal: He called him out of the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Avuzhiluo outside the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembled company.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅慚其臣下，大怒曰：「帳中何不教我拜，而辱我於大眾！」

translations.literal: Avuzhiluo, shamed before his subjects, said in great anger, "Why did you not teach me to bow inside the tent, but instead humiliate me before the great crowd!"
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed before his followers, Avuzhiluo flew into a rage: "Why did you not have me bow inside the tent, but humiliate me before the whole assembly?"

sentences.zh: 奪長生等獻物，囚之叢石之中，兵脅之曰：「汝能為我臣則活，如其不降，殺汝！」

translations.literal: He seized the tribute objects of Changsheng and the others and imprisoned them among piled stones. Soldiers threatened them, saying, "If you can become my subjects you will live; if you do not submit, you will be killed!"
translations.idiomatic: He confiscated their tribute gifts and imprisoned them among the rocks. Armed men threatened them: "Become my subjects and you shall live. Refuse, and you die."

sentences.zh: 長生與于提瞋目厲聲責之曰：「豈有天子使人拜汝夷，我寧為魏鬼，不為汝臣！」

translations.literal: Changsheng and Yu Ti glared with wide eyes and in fierce voices rebuked them, saying, "How could an envoy of the Son of Heaven bow to you barbarians! I would rather be a ghost of Wei than your subject!"
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng and Yu Ti glared and shouted their rebuke: "Shall an envoy of the Son of Heaven bow to you barbarians? I would rather be a ghost of Wei than your subject!"

sentences.zh: 至羅彌怒，絕其飲食。

translations.literal: Avuzhiluo grew still angrier and cut off their food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Avuzhiluo's fury only grew, and he cut off their food and drink.

sentences.zh: 從行者三十人皆降，至羅乃給以肉酪，惟長生與提不從，乃各分徙之。

translations.literal: The thirty who had accompanied them all submitted; Avuzhiluo then gave them meat and curds, but only Changsheng and Ti would not comply, and he had them separated and exiled each to a different place.
translations.idiomatic: All thirty of their attendants submitted, and Avuzhiluo gave them meat and curds. Only Changsheng and Yu Ti refused, so he had them separated and sent to different places of exile.

sentences.zh: 積三歲，乃得還。

translations.literal: After three years they were at last able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Three years passed before they were able to return.

sentences.zh: 高祖以長生等守節遠同蘇武，甚嘉之，拜長生河內太守，于提隴西太守，並賜爵五等男。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Changsheng and the others upheld their integrity in a manner far matching Su Wu, greatly commended them, appointing Changsheng administrator of Henei and Yu Ti administrator of Longxi, and granting both the fifth-rank baronetcy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen held that in keeping their integrity Changsheng and his companions rivaled Su Wu of old, and he greatly honored them. Changsheng was appointed administrator of Henei, Yu Ti administrator of Longxi, and both were enfeoffed as fifth-rank barons.

sentences.zh: 從者皆為令長。

translations.literal: Those who had accompanied them were all made magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Their attendants were all appointed district magistrates.

sentences.zh: 馬八龍，武邑武強人也。

translations.literal: Ma Balong was a man of Wuqiang in Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Balong came from Wuqiang in Wuyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 輕財重義。

translations.literal: He held wealth lightly and valued righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He held wealth lightly and prized righteousness.

sentences.zh: 友人武遂縣尹靈哲在軍喪亡，八龍聞即奔赴，負屍而歸，以家財殯葬，為制緦服。

translations.literal: His friend Yin Lingzhe, magistrate of Wusui county, died on campaign; when Balong heard, he rushed at once, carried the corpse on his back and returned, buried him at family expense, and wore the hemp of the lowest mourning grade.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend Yin Lingzhe, magistrate of Wusui county, died on campaign, Balong hurried to the scene at once, carried the body home on his back, buried him at his own expense, and wore the coarsest grade of mourning.

sentences.zh: 撫其孤遺，恩如所生。

translations.literal: He nurtured the orphan left behind with affection as though the child were his own.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the orphan left behind with the same devotion he would have shown his own child.

sentences.zh: 州郡表列，詔表門閭。

translations.literal: The province and commandery reported and listed him; an edict ordered a placard at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery reported his conduct, and an edict ordered a commemorative placard posted at his gate.

sentences.zh: 門文愛，汲郡山陽人也。

translations.literal: Men Wen'ai was a man of Shanyang in Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Men Wen'ai came from Shanyang in Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 早孤，供養伯父母以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he supported his uncle and aunt with filial care and was known for it.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he supported his uncle and aunt with filial devotion and was famed for it.

sentences.zh: 伯父亡，服未終，伯母又亡。

translations.literal: When his uncle died, mourning was not yet finished before his aunt also died.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle died, and before that mourning was complete his aunt died as well.

sentences.zh: 文愛居喪，持服六年，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: Wen'ai dwelt in mourning, wore the garments for six years, and his grief wasted him until only bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'ai observed mourning for six years, his grief so consuming that he was wasted to bone.

sentences.zh: 鄉人魏中賢等相與標其孝義。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Wei Zhongxian and others together commended his filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Wei Zhongxian and others jointly commended his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 晁清，遼東人也。

translations.literal: Chao Qing was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Qing came from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 祖暉，濟州刺史、潁川公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was inspector of Ji province and Duke of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had served as inspector of Ji province and Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 清襲祖爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: Qing inherited his grandfather's title, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Qing inherited his grandfather's rank, which by regulation was reduced one step to marquis.

sentences.zh: 為梁城戍將。

translations.literal: He served as garrison commander of Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as garrison commander of Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍攻圍，糧盡城陷，清抗節不屈，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan besieged him; when grain was exhausted the city fell. Qing upheld his integrity and would not submit, and was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan besieged the city and supplies ran out, the fortress fell. Qing held to his integrity and refused to yield, and the enemy killed him.

sentences.zh: 世宗褒美，贈樂陵太守，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Shizong praised and commended him, posthumously granting him administrator of Leling, with the posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu honored him posthumously as administrator of Leling with the posthumous name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 子榮賓襲。

translations.literal: His son Rongbin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongbin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 劉侯仁，豫州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Houran was a man of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Houran came from Yu province.

sentences.zh: 城人白早生殺刺史司馬悅，據城南叛。

translations.literal: A townsman, Bai Zaosheng, killed the inspector Sima Yue, seized the south of the city, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Bai Zaosheng killed the provincial inspector Sima Yue, seized the southern part of the city, and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 悅息朏，走投侯仁。

translations.literal: Yue's son Fei fled in distress to seek Houran.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Fei fled for his life to Liu Houran.

sentences.zh: 賊雖重加購募，又嚴其捶撻，侯仁終無漏泄，朏遂免禍。

translations.literal: Although the bandits repeatedly increased the reward for his capture and strictly beat and flogged him, Houran never leaked anything, and Fei thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rebels raised the bounty on his head and tortured him severely, Houran never betrayed the boy, and Fei was spared.

sentences.zh: 事寧，有司奏其操行，請免府籍，敍一小縣，詔可。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the responsible offices memorialized his conduct and requested that he be removed from the prefectural register and appointed to a small county; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, the authorities reported his conduct and asked that he be struck from the prefectural rolls and given a minor county post; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 石祖興，常山九門人也。

translations.literal: Shi Zuxing was a man of Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zuxing came from Jiumen in Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 太守田文彪、縣令和真等喪亡，祖興自出家絹二百餘匹，營護喪事。

translations.literal: When the grand administrator Tian Wenbiao, the magistrate He Zhen, and others died, Zuxing himself contributed more than two hundred bolts of silk from his household to arrange and oversee their funerals.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Administrator Tian Wenbiao, Magistrate He Zhen, and others died in office, Zuxing gave more than two hundred bolts of silk from his own household to see to their burials.

sentences.zh: 州郡表列，高祖嘉之，賜爵二級，為上造。

translations.literal: The province and commandery reported and listed him; Gaozu commended him and granted two ranks of nobility, making him Shangzao.
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery reported his conduct. Emperor Xiaowen praised him, raised his noble rank by two steps, and enfeoffed him as Shangzao.

sentences.zh: 後拜寧陵令，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed magistrate of Ningling and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed magistrate of Ningling, where he died.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李韶奏其節義，請加贈諡，以奬來者，靈太后令如所奏。

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shao memorialized his integrity and righteousness and requested a posthumous title to encourage those who would come after; Empress Dowager Ling ordered that it be done as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao, Minister of Personnel, memorialized Zuxing's loyalty and asked that a posthumous title be granted to encourage others. Empress Dowager Ling ordered that it be done as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 有司諡曰恭。

translations.literal: The responsible offices gave the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 邵洪哲，上谷沮陽人也。

translations.literal: Shao Hongzhe was a man of Juyang in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Hongzhe came from Juyang in Shanggu commandery.

sentences.zh: 縣令范道榮先自朐城歸款以除縣令，[5]道榮鄉人徐孔明，妄經公府，訟道榮非勳，道榮坐除名。

translations.literal: The magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier submitted from Qucheng in allegiance and was relieved of the magistracy;[5] Daorong's fellow townsman Xu Kongming falsely petitioned the public offices, suing that Daorong had no merit, and Daorong was dismissed and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier surrendered from Qucheng and been relieved of his post.[5] A fellow townsman, Xu Kongming, lodged a false complaint at the capital that Daorong had no merit, and Daorong was dismissed and struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 羇旅孤貧，不能自理。

translations.literal: A wanderer, alone and poor, he could not manage for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Destitute and far from home, he could not manage on his own.

sentences.zh: 洪哲不勝義憤，遂代道榮詣京師，明申曲直。

translations.literal: Hongzhe, unable to bear his righteous indignation, thereupon went to the capital on Daorong's behalf and clearly set forth right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhe, moved by righteous indignation, went to the capital in Daorong's stead and laid out the rights and wrongs of the case.

sentences.zh: 經歷寒暑，不憚劬勞，道榮卒得復雪。

translations.literal: Passing through cold and heat, he did not shrink from toil, and Daorong at last had his honor restored.
translations.idiomatic: Through winter and summer he endured the hardship without complaint, until Daorong's name was cleared at last.

sentences.zh: 又北鎮反亂，道榮孤單，無所歸附。

translations.literal: When the northern garrisons rebelled, Daorong was alone with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern garrisons rose in revolt, Daorong was utterly alone, with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 洪哲兄伯川復率鄉人來相迎接，送達幽州。

translations.literal: Hongzhe's elder brother Bochuan again led the townspeople to meet and welcome him, escorting him as far as You province.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhe's elder brother Bochuan again led their fellow townspeople to receive Daorong and escort him safely to You province.

sentences.zh: 道榮感其誠節，訴省申聞。

translations.literal: Daorong, moved by their sincere integrity, appealed to the provincial authorities to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved by their loyalty, Daorong petitioned the provincial authorities to report their conduct.

sentences.zh: 詔下州郡，標其里閭。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the provinces and commanderies to post placards at their hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered placards posted at their hamlets throughout the provinces.

sentences.zh: 王榮世，陽平館陶人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rongshi was a man of Guantao in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rongshi came from Guantao in Yangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 為三城戍主、方城縣子。

translations.literal: He served as garrison commander of Sancheng and Baron of Fangcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He served as garrison commander of Sancheng and held the title Baron of Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍攻圍，力窮知不可全，乃先焚府庫，後殺妻妾。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan besieged him and his strength was exhausted, knowing he could not preserve all, he first burned the treasury and then killed his wife and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan besieged the fortress and resistance failed, seeing that all could not be saved, he burned the treasury first and then killed his wife and concubines.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷城，與戍副鄧元興等俱以不屈被害。

translations.literal: When the bandits took the city, he and the deputy garrison commander Deng Yuanxing and others were all killed for refusing to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he and his deputy Deng Yuanxing and others were killed for refusing to yield.

sentences.zh: 肅宗下詔褒美忠節，進榮世爵為伯，贈齊州刺史；

translations.literal: Suzong issued an edict praising their loyal integrity, promoted Rongshi's title to marquis, and posthumously granted him inspector of Qi province;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong issued an edict praising their loyalty, promoted Rongshi's rank to marquis, and posthumously appointed him inspector of Qi province;

sentences.zh: 元興開國子，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanxing was granted the founding viscountcy and posthumously made inspector of Luo province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing was enfeoffed as a founding viscount and posthumously appointed inspector of Luo province.

sentences.zh: 胡小虎，河南河陰人也。

translations.literal: Hu Xiaohu was a man of Heyin in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiaohu came from Heyin in Henan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有武氣。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed martial spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Even in youth he had a warrior's spirit.

sentences.zh: 正光末，為統軍於晉壽。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era he served as army commander at Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang period he commanded troops at Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，蕭衍將樊文熾等寇邊，益州刺史邴虬遣長史和安固守小劍，文熾圍之。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era the generals of Xiao Yan, Fan Wenchì and others, raided the frontier; the inspector of Yi province, Bing Qiu, sent his chief clerk He An to hold Xiaojian firmly, and Wenchì besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang period Xiao Yan's generals Fan Wenchì and others raided the border. Bing Qiu, inspector of Yi province, sent his chief clerk He An to hold Xiaojian, and Wenchì laid siege.

sentences.zh: 虬命小虎與統軍崔珍寶同往防拒。

translations.literal: Qiu ordered Xiaohu and the army commander Cui Zhenbao to go together to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu ordered Xiaohu and the army commander Cui Zhenbao to march out and resist.

sentences.zh: 文熾掩襲小虎、珍寶，並擒之。

translations.literal: Wenchì launched a surprise attack on Xiaohu and Zhenbao and captured them both.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchì ambushed Xiaohu and Zhenbao and took them both prisoner.

sentences.zh: 文熾攻小劍未陷，乃將珍寶至城下，使謂和安曰：「南軍強盛，北救不來，豈若歸款，取其富貴。」

translations.literal: Wenchì had not yet taken Xiaojian, so he brought Zhenbao to the foot of the wall and had him say to He An, "The southern army is strong; northern relief will not come—would it not be better to submit and win wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiaojian fell, Wenchì brought Zhenbao to the wall and had him call to He An: "The southern army is strong and northern relief will not come. Why not surrender and win wealth and rank?"

sentences.zh: 和安命射之，乃退。

translations.literal: He An ordered archers to shoot at him, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He An ordered his men to shoot at them, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復逼小虎與和安交言，小虎乃慷慨謂安曰：「我柵不防，為賊所虜。

translations.literal: They again forced Xiaohu to speak with He An. Xiaohu then said with fervor to An, "My palisade was not defended and I was captured by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They forced Xiaohu to speak with He An again. Xiaohu cried out to him: "My camp was unprepared and the enemy took me.

sentences.zh: 觀其兵士，勢不足言，努力堅守。

translations.literal: Looking at their soldiers, their strength is not worth mentioning—strive to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Their troops are nothing to fear. Hold the fortress with all your strength.

sentences.zh: 魏行臺傳梁州遣將已至。」

translations.literal: The Wei mobile headquarters in Liang province has already sent generals—they have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei field headquarters in Liang province has already dispatched reinforcements—they are here."

sentences.zh: [6]賊以刀毆擊，言不得終，遂害之。

translations.literal: [6] The bandits struck him with blades; he could not finish his words and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: [6] The enemy beat him with blades before he could finish, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 三軍無不歎其壯節，哀其死亡。

translations.literal: Throughout the three armies none failed to admire his stalwart integrity and mourn his death.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army marveled at his courage and mourned his death.

sentences.zh: 賊尋奔敗，禽其次將蕭世澄、陳文緒等一十一人。

translations.literal: The bandits soon fled in defeat, and eleven of their subordinate generals, including Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu, were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy soon broke and fled, and eleven of their officers, including Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu, were captured.

sentences.zh: 行臺魏子建壯其氣概，啟以世澄購其屍柩，乃獲骸骨歸葬。

translations.literal: The mobile headquarters commander Wei Zijian admired his spirit; he memorialized that Shicheng be ransomed for his coffin, and the remains were obtained and returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Field commander Wei Zijian admired his spirit and petitioned to exchange the captive Shicheng for his body. The remains were recovered and buried with honor.

sentences.zh: 孫道登，彭城呂縣人也。

translations.literal: Sun Daodeng was a man of Lü county in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daodeng came from Lü county in Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 永安初，為蕭衍將韋休等所虜，面縛臨刃，巡遠村塢，令其招降鄉曲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was captured by the generals of Xiao Yan, Wei Xiu and others; bound facing the blade, he was led through distant villages and stockades and ordered to induce the local people to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yong'an period he was taken prisoner by Xiao Yan's general Wei Xiu and others. Bound and marched at sword-point through distant hamlets, he was forced to urge the countryside to surrender.

sentences.zh: 道登厲聲唱呼：「但當努力，賊無所能。」

translations.literal: Daodeng shouted in a fierce voice, "Only strive with all your might—the bandits can do nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng shouted at the top of his voice: "Stand firm! The enemy can do nothing!"

sentences.zh: 賊遂屠戮之。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon slaughtered him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又荊州被圍，行臺宗靈恩遣使宗女等四人入城曉喻，為賊將所獲，執女等巡城，令其改辭。

translations.literal: Also, when Jing province was besieged, the mobile headquarters commander Zong Ling'en sent four envoys, including Zong Nü, into the city to instruct and persuade; they were seized by an enemy general, who led Nü and the others around the wall and ordered them to change their words.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing province was besieged, field commander Zong Ling'en sent four envoys, including Zong Nü, into the city to rally the defenders. An enemy general seized them, paraded them along the walls, and ordered them to change their message.

sentences.zh: 女等大言：「天軍垂至，堅守莫降。」

translations.literal: Nü and the others cried loudly, "The heavenly army is about to arrive—hold firm and do not submit!"
translations.idiomatic: They shouted: "The imperial army is almost here. Hold firm and do not surrender!"

sentences.zh: 賊忿，各刳其腹，然後斬首。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger disemboweled each of them and then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: In fury the enemy disemboweled each of them and then cut off their heads.

sentences.zh: 二州表其節義，道登等並賜五品郡、五等子爵，聽子弟承襲。

translations.literal: The two provinces reported their integrity and righteousness; Daodeng and the others were all granted fifth-rank commandery posts and fifth-rank viscountcies, and their sons and younger brothers were permitted to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Both provinces reported their loyalty. Daodeng and the others were granted fifth-rank commandery posts and fifth-rank viscountcies, with permission for their sons and brothers to inherit.

sentences.zh: 遣使詣所在弔祭。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to their locales to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to their home districts to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 李几，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Li Ji was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji came from Anping in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 七世共居同財，家有二十二房，一百九十八口，長幼濟濟，風禮著聞，至於作役，卑幼競進。

translations.literal: Seven generations dwelt together and shared property; the household had twenty-two branches and one hundred ninety-eight mouths; old and young were numerous, custom and ritual were renowned, and when there was labor to be done the younger ones vied to take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations lived together under one roof, sharing property across twenty-two branches and one hundred ninety-eight souls. Old and young alike were numerous, their household famed for ritual propriety, and whenever work arose the younger members vied to take the lead.

sentences.zh: 鄉里嗟美，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The village sighed in admiration and posted a placard at their gate.
translations.idiomatic: The countryside marveled at them, and a commemorative placard was posted at their gate.

sentences.zh: 張安祖，河陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Anzu was a man of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Anzu came from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 襲世爵山北侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary title Marquis of Shanbei.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary title Marquis of Shanbei.

sentences.zh: 時有元承貴，曾為河陽令，家貧，且赴尚書求選，逢天寒甚，遂凍死路側。

translations.literal: At that time there was Yuan Chenggui, who had once been magistrate of Heyang; his family was poor, and as he was going to the Ministry to seek appointment, he encountered severe cold and froze to death by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a certain Yuan Chenggui, formerly magistrate of Heyang, was poor and on his way to the Ministry to seek an appointment when bitter cold killed him by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 一子年幼，停屍門巷，棺斂無託。

translations.literal: He had one young son; the corpse lay in the lane with no one to provide coffin and encoffinment.
translations.idiomatic: He left a young son; the body lay in the lane with no one to provide a coffin or burial.

sentences.zh: 安祖悲哭盡禮，買木為棺，手自營作，斂殯周給。

translations.literal: Anzu mourned with full rites, bought wood for a coffin, worked on it with his own hands, and provided complete encoffinment and burial.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu mourned him with full rites, bought wood and built the coffin with his own hands, and saw to a complete burial.

sentences.zh: 朝野嘉歎。

translations.literal: Court and countryside praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 尚書聞奏，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The Ministry heard and memorialized; a placard was posted at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry reported the matter, and a commemorative placard was posted at his gate.

sentences.zh: 王閭，北海密人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lü was a man of Mi in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lü came from Mi in Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 數世同居，有百口。

translations.literal: Several generations dwelt together, with a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Several generations lived together under one roof, a household of a hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 又太山劉業興四世同居，魯郡蓋儁六世同居，並共財產，家門雍睦。

translations.literal: Also, Liu Yexing of Taishan dwelt together for four generations; Gai Jun of Lu commandery for six generations—all shared property, and their households were harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yexing of Taishan lived together for four generations; Gai Jun of Lu commandery for six. All shared property, and their households were harmonious.

sentences.zh: 鄉里敬異。

translations.literal: Their villages revered and marveled at them.
translations.idiomatic: Their neighbors held them in awe and admiration.

sentences.zh: 有司申奏，皆標門閭。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized, and placards were posted at all their gates.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported their conduct, and commemorative placards were posted at each of their gates.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：于什門等或臨危不撓，視死如歸；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Yu Shenmen and the others, some facing peril without yielding, regarded death as returning home;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yu Shenmen and his companions—some faced peril without flinching and met death as though going home;

sentences.zh: 或赴險如夷，惟義所在。

translations.literal: some went into danger as though onto level ground, wherever righteousness lay.
translations.idiomatic: others went into danger as onto level ground, wherever righteousness called.

sentences.zh: 其大則光國隆家，其小則損己利物。

translations.literal: In the large case they glorified the state and elevated the clan; in the small they harmed themselves to benefit others.
translations.idiomatic: At their grandest they brought glory to the state and honor to their clans; at the least they harmed themselves to benefit others.

sentences.zh: 故其盛烈所著，與河海而爭流；

translations.literal: Therefore the splendor they achieved vies in flow with rivers and seas;
translations.idiomatic: Their great deeds therefore vie in splendor with rivers and seas;

sentences.zh: 峻節所標，共松栢而俱茂。

translations.literal: the lofty integrity they marked shares flourishing with pine and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: the integrity they embodied flourishes alongside pine and cypress.

sentences.zh: 並蹈履之所致，身歿名立，豈徒然哉。

translations.literal: All were brought about by treading the path; when the body perished the name was established—how could it be in vain?
translations.idiomatic: All this came of living the path they chose: though their bodies perished, their names endure. Surely it was not for nothing.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十七 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，卷末附宋人校語

translations.literal: Weishu juan 87: various editions' tables of contents mark this juan "deficient"; Song-dynasty collation notes are appended at the end of the juan.
translations.idiomatic: Weishu, juan 87: various editions' tables of contents mark this chapter as "deficient"; Song-dynasty collation notes are appended at the end.

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Entered under textual verification in the Palace Edition〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Entered under textual verification in the Palace Edition〉

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書節義傳亡。」

translations.literal: It states: "Wei Shou's biography of Integrity and Righteousness is lost."
translations.idiomatic: It states: "Wei Shou's 'Integrity and Righteousness' biography is lost."

sentences.zh: 按傳序與北史卷八五節義傳序不同，當自原序刪節。

translations.literal: According to this, the preface to the biography differs from the preface to the Integrity and Righteousness biography in Beishi juan 85; it must have been abridged from the original preface.
translations.idiomatic: The preface here differs from that in Beishi, juan 85, and must have been abridged from the original.

sentences.zh: 諸傳中只于什門傳稍詳於北史，王玄威傳所載詔書有溢出北史所載的文句，其他諸傳偶有一二字溢出，大抵全同北史。

translations.literal: Among the various biographies only the Yu Shenmen biography is somewhat more detailed than the Beishi; the edict recorded in the Wang Xuanwei biography has sentences exceeding what the Beishi records; the other biographies occasionally have a character or two in excess—on the whole they are entirely the same as the Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Of the biographies, only Yu Shenmen's is somewhat fuller than in the Beishi; Wang Xuanwei's includes edict language not found there; others differ by a word or two at most. On the whole they match the Beishi almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 諸人事迹本無可述，原文也必甚簡略。

translations.literal: The deeds of these men in themselves had little to relate; the original text must also have been very brief.
translations.idiomatic: These men's deeds were in themselves slight; the original text must have been very brief.

sentences.zh: 此卷多數傳文全同北史，或由於所據的史鈔和北史都是直錄魏書，非必以北史補。

translations.literal: Most of the biographical texts in this juan are entirely the same as the Beishi; this may be because the historical excerpts on which both are based directly copied the Weishu, and it is not necessarily that the Beishi was used to supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Most of this chapter matches the Beishi verbatim, perhaps because both drew on excerpts copied directly from the Weishu rather than because the Beishi was used to fill gaps.

sentences.zh: 大義重於至聞自日人 殿本考證云：「首九字訛舛，不可推尋。」

translations.literal: Great righteousness is heavier than the utmost fame, since the day of men: the Palace Edition textual verification states, "The first nine characters are corrupt and cannot be reconstructed."
translations.idiomatic: On "Great righteousness outweighs the utmost fame, since the day of men": the Palace Edition notes that the first nine characters are corrupt and cannot be reconstructed.

sentences.zh: 歷二十四年 通鑑卷一二二

translations.literal: Twenty-four years passed: Zizhi tongjian juan 122
translations.idiomatic: "Twenty-four years passed": Zizhi tongjian, juan 122

sentences.zh: 〈三八五三頁〉
記于什門還魏於元嘉十一年

translations.literal: records Yu Shenmen's return to Wei in the eleventh year of Yuanjia
translations.idiomatic: records Yu Shenmen's return to Wei in the eleventh year of Yuanjia

sentences.zh: 〈魏延和三年

translations.literal: 〈Yan Yanhe year 3
translations.idiomatic: 〈Northern Wei Yanhe year 3

sentences.zh: (四三四)〉，
「二十四」作「二十一」。

translations.literal: "twenty-four" is written as "twenty-one."
translations.idiomatic: reading "twenty-four" as "twenty-one."

sentences.zh: 考異云：「後魏本紀

translations.literal: Kaoyi states: "The Later Wei basic annals
translations.idiomatic: Kaoyi notes: "The Later Wei annals

sentences.zh: 〈卷三〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 3〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 3〉

sentences.zh: 神瑞元年

translations.literal: first year of Shenrui
translations.idiomatic: first year of Shenrui

sentences.zh: 〈四一四〉
八月遣于什門招諭馮跋，至此年二十一年矣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yu Shenmen was sent to summon and instruct Feng Ba; by this year twenty-one years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yu Shenmen was sent to summon Feng Ba; by this year twenty-one years had elapsed.

sentences.zh: 若二十四年，乃在太延三年，而太延二年馮氏亡矣。」

translations.literal: If it were twenty-four years, that would fall in the third year of Taiyan, yet in the second year of Taiyan the Feng clan had perished."
translations.idiomatic: If it were twenty-four years, that would place the return in Taiyan year 3, but the Feng state fell in Taiyan year 2."

sentences.zh: 按傳稱「馮文通上表稱臣，乃送什門歸」，卷四上世祖紀上延和三年三月記「文通遣尚書高顒上表稱藩」，故通鑑置於是年。

translations.literal: According to the biography, "Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent home"; juan 4A, Annals of Shizu, upper, third month of the third year of Yanhe records "Wentong sent the Master of Writing Gao Yong to submit a memorial declaring himself a vassal," hence the Zizhi tongjian places it in that year.
translations.idiomatic: The biography says that "Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent home." Shizu annals, juan 4A, Yanhe third year, third month, records that "Wentong sent Master of Writing Gao Yong to submit a memorial declaring himself a vassal"; hence the Zizhi tongjian places the return in that year.

sentences.zh: 疑「二十四」當作「二十一」。

translations.literal: It is suspected that "twenty-four" should read "twenty-one."
translations.idiomatic: "Twenty-four" is probably a mistake for "twenty-one."

sentences.zh: 河中蒲坂人也 北史卷八五石文德傳「河中蒲坂」作「中山蒲陰」。

translations.literal: A man of Puban in Hezhong: Beishi juan 85, Shi Wende biography, reads "Puban in Hezhong" as "Puyin in Zhongshan."
translations.idiomatic: "A man of Puban in Hezhong": Beishi, juan 85, Shi Wende biography, reads "Puban in Hezhong" as "Puyin in Zhongshan."

sentences.zh: 按蒲坂自來屬河東郡，魏也無「河中」郡名。

translations.literal: According to this, Puban has always belonged to Hedong commandery, and Wei also had no commandery named "Hezhong."
translations.idiomatic: Puban has always belonged to Hedong commandery; Northern Wei had no commandery called "Hezhong."

sentences.zh: 卷一０六上地形志上定州北平郡有蒲陰縣，北平郡乃孝昌二年分中山置。

translations.literal: Juan 106A, Treatise on Geography, upper, Dingzhou, Beiping commandery, has Puyin county; Beiping commandery was established in the second year of Xiaochang by partitioning Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Geography treatise, juan 106A, lists Puyin county in Beiping commandery, Dingzhou; Beiping was carved from Zhongshan in Xiaochang year 2.

sentences.zh: 若非「中」為「東」字之訛，則「河中蒲坂」為「中山蒲陰」之訛。

translations.literal: If "zhong" is not a corruption of "dong," then "Puban in Hezhong" is a corruption of "Puyin in Zhongshan."
translations.idiomatic: Unless "zhong" is a corruption of "dong," "Puban in Hezhong" is a corruption of "Puyin in Zhongshan."

sentences.zh: 縣令范道榮先自朐城歸款以除縣令 諸本「朐」作「眴」，北史卷八五邵洪哲傳作「眗」。

translations.literal: The magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier submitted from Qucheng in allegiance and was relieved of the magistracy: various editions write "qu" as "shun"; Beishi juan 85, Shao Hongzhe biography, writes "ju."
translations.idiomatic: On "Magistrate Fan Daorong submitted from Qucheng": various editions read qu as shun; Beishi, juan 85, Shao Hongzhe biography, has ju.

sentences.zh: 冊府卷一三八

translations.literal: Cefu yuangui juan 138
translations.idiomatic: Cefu yuangui, juan 138

sentences.zh: 〈一六六六頁〉、
卷八０三

translations.literal: juan 803
translations.idiomatic: juan 803

sentences.zh: 〈九五四八頁〉
並作「朐」。

translations.literal: Both read "qu."
translations.idiomatic: Both read "qu."

sentences.zh: 按「朐城歸款」事見卷八世宗紀永平四年四月、卷四七盧淵附盧昶傳、卷九八蕭衍傳，「朐城」亦作「朐山」。

translations.literal: According to this, the affair of "Qucheng's submission in allegiance" appears in juan 8, Annals of Shizong, fourth month of the fourth year of Yongping; juan 47, Lu Yuan with appended biography of Lu Chang; and juan 98, Xiao Yan biography; "Qucheng" is also written as "Qushan."
translations.idiomatic: The affair of "Qucheng's surrender in allegiance" appears in Shizong annals, juan 8, Yongping fourth year, fourth month; Lu Yuan with appended biography of Lu Chang, juan 47; and the biography of Xiao Yan, juan 98. The place name "Qucheng" is also written "Qushan."

sentences.zh: 「眴」「眗」都是「朐」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Shun" and "ju" are both corruptions of "qu"; the text is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Both "shun" and "ju" are corruptions of "qu"; the text is emended accordingly.
